{"metadata":{"description":"Run a DeepSeek Harness session against a WSL distro: ctx.shell, ctx.fs and the GUI terminal served from inside the distro, sandboxed with bubblewrap","id":"gh:1401070542","install_available":true,"language":"JavaScript","name":"dsh-plugin-wsl-env","slug":"Big-Dao/dsh-plugin-wsl-env","topics":["cordis","deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-plugin","windows","wsl2"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Run a DeepSeek Harness session against a WSL distro: ctx.shell, ctx.fs and the GUI terminal served f"},{"id":"p1s2","text":"rom inside the distro, sandboxed with bubblewrap"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-plugin-wsl-env"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"**English** · 中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"A DeepSeek Harness plugin that opens the project workspace inside a WSL 2 distribution on Windows."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"The harness process stays on Windows. Command execution, shell scripts and file access all run in th"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"e distro's Linux environment for the full Linux shell toolchain. No helper service or daemon is inst"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"alled, no port is opened, and confined commands run under `bubblewrap`."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"Windows + WSL 2 only."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"**New here?** Start with docs/QUICKSTART.md — prerequisites, recipes and the compatibility table."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"## Do I need this plugin?"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"If the harness itself can run in the distro, it is simpler **not** to use this
plugin: install the C"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"LI there and run it from the distro's shell. No UNC paths,
no 9p round trips, no Windows-to-distro a"},{"id":"p9s3","text":"ere and run it from the distro's shell. No UNC paths,
no 9p round trips, no Windows-to-distro agent."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"Use this plugin when the harness has to stay on Windows:"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"| Your setup | What to use |"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"| Work happens inside WSL; a terminal or browser UI is enough | the CLI installed in the distro |
| "},{"id":"p13s2","text":"You want the Windows desktop app, with commands and files in the distro | this plugin |
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"## Why this plugin"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"A Windows coding tool that works on WSL projects has three options: run the whole tool inside the di"},{"id":"p15s2","text":"stro, connect to a helper server inside the distro, or let the plugin provide the distro environment"},{"id":"p15s3","text":". This plugin is the third option. One workflow covers both kinds of session, with the distro's real"},{"id":"p15s4","text":" tools and the command sandbox intact."},{"id":"p16s1","text":"- **Real Linux environment.** Commands run in the distro's own login shell. Its `PATH`, `nvm`, `carg"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"o`, `pyenv` and rc files apply. File tools access distro paths through an in-distro agent; the backi"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"ng filesystem depends on the path.
- **No service in the distro.** There is no helper server, no dae"},{"id":"p16s4","text":"mon and no listening port. The only persisted artifact is a content-addressed copy of the native age"},{"id":"p16s5","text":"nt in `~/.cache/dsh-wsl/agent/`.
- **Sandboxed by default.** Confined commands run under `bubblewrap"},{"id":"p16s6","text":"` inside the distro. If `bubblewrap` is missing, the command fails; it does not run unconfined.
- **"},{"id":"p16s7","text":"Per-session.** A session opened on a distro folder gets the distro environment. A session opened on "},{"id":"p16s8","text":"a Windows folder keeps the normal Windows tools. Both can run in one harness process.
- **Integrated"},{"id":"p16s9","text":" with the GUI.** The folder picker lists installed distros, the terminal opens a shell in the distro"},{"id":"p16s10","text":", and the model can see listening ports. A doctor button in the composer runs the environment diagno"},{"id":"p16s11","text":"sis as a `/wsl-doctor` command — host-side, no model turn — and the session-start preflight announce"},{"id":"p16s12","text":"s the environment verdict on every session."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"### Why Linux, not PowerShell"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"Most coding agents learn from Linux-first material, and most open-source toolchains are built and te"},{"id":"p18s2","text":"sted on Linux first. Asking an agent to work through a Windows shell adds a translation layer on eve"},{"id":"p18s3","text":"Linux first. Asking an agent to work through a Windows shell adds a translation layer on every call:"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"- **Training prior.** Examples, CI scripts, Dockerfiles and most public answers use POSIX shells and"},{"id":"p19s2","text":" GNU tools. A model's first instinct is `bash`, not PowerShell.
- **Toolchain support.** Node, Pytho"},{"id":"p19s3","text":"n, Rust, Go, C/C++ and most build systems are validated on Linux first. Windows support is often a p"},{"id":"p19s4","text":"ort with different quoting, paths, line endings and file locking.
- **Shell semantics.** PowerShell "},{"id":"p19s5","text":"and `cmd` differ from POSIX in quoting, escaping, pipelines, environment variables, exit codes and p"},{"id":"p19s6","text":"ath separators. Mixing the two produces errors that look like model mistakes.
- **Environment drift."},{"id":"p19s7","text":"** Windows setups vary by PowerShell version, execution policy, PATH and installed tools. Linux envi"},{"id":"p19s8","text":"ronments are easier to reproduce and containerize."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"The result is more failed commands, more retries and more time spent on syntax instead of the task. "},{"id":"p20s2","text":"Generated code is affected too: shell snippets, build commands and CI-style one-liners are usually w"},{"id":"p20s3","text":"ritten for POSIX, and the distro is where they run unchanged. A real Linux login shell removes that "},{"id":"p20s4","text":"translation layer. Modern PowerShell and Windows-native toolchains narrow the gap, but the default p"},{"id":"p20s5","text":"rior and most project scripts still assume POSIX."},{"id":"p21s1","text":"This plugin keeps the GUI on Windows and moves only the execution environment into the distro, so th"},{"id":"p21s2","text":"e agent gets the shell that its training and the toolchain both assume."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"## Requirements"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"- Windows 10 or 11 with WSL 2 and at least one distro.
- `bubblewrap` in the distro. It is required."},{"id":"p23s2","text":"
- systemd in the distro for the default session sandbox: set `[boot] systemd=true` in `/etc/wsl.con"},{"id":"p23s3","text":"f`, restart WSL, then run `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` once. Without systemd, set `sessionSandbo"},{"id":"p23s4","text":"x` to `auto` (the scope when available, otherwise per-command confinement) or explicit `false` on bo"},{"id":"p23s5","text":"th `wsl-shell` and `wsl-fs`.
- Optional: `ripgrep` for search, `git` for change snapshots, `inotify-"},{"id":"p23s6","text":"tools` for file watching."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"No Node.js is required inside the distro."},{"id":"p25s1","text":"## Architecture"},{"id":"p26s1","text":"One harness process can serve Windows-folder and distro-folder sessions at the same time. Services a"},{"id":"p26s2","text":"ttach at two levels:"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"- `wsl-shell` runs commands through one resident agent inside a systemd user scope. The agent is the"},{"id":"p28s2","text":" packaged static-musl `dsh-wsl-agent` for the distro's architecture (`x86_64` or `aarch64`), with th"},{"id":"p28s3","text":"e shell agent as fallback. Each command runs in the login shell under a `bubblewrap` mount profile. "},{"id":"p28s4","text":"The scope outlives the command, so background servers survive and `ps` sees the session. With `sessi"},{"id":"p28s5","text":"onSandbox: false`, the agent stays per distro and each command gets its own profile.
- `wsl-fs` serv"},{"id":"p28s6","text":"es reads and writes through the same in-distro agent. Confined writes run in a long-lived agent whos"},{"id":"p28s7","text":"e mount profile matches the policy, so the kernel enforces the write boundary. There is no host-side"},{"id":"p28s8","text":" file fallback: if the agent is unavailable, file operations fail.
- The GUI file tree and previews "},{"id":"p28s9","text":"are the shipped `workspace-files` row, not a plugin replacement: its client half is the browser `fil"},{"id":"p28s10","text":"e` provider. It reads WSL paths through the routed root filesystem, so it stays distro-side, at the "},{"id":"p28s11","text":"cost of a few extra agent round trips.
- App-level services route by path. A distro UNC path goes to"},{"id":"p28s12","text":" the distro; a Windows drive path stays on the host. See docs/root-fs-routing.md."}],"truncated":true}
